To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insulin signaling events promote the removal of eif4E-bound Nonsense-mediated mRNA Decay targets.
insulin signaling enhances eIF4E-dependent nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (eNMD) through the phosphorylation of AKT, leading to the colocalization and interaction of eIF4F and UPF1 in mammalian cells.
insulin signaling enhances eIF4E-dependent NMD by promoting the binding of UPF1 to eIF4F-bound PTC-containing mRNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of mRNA stability by NMD.
the interplay between insulin signaling and the regulation of translation and NMD.
the regulation of translation by insulin and its effect on NMD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin stimulation enhances translation, leading to the colocalization and binding of UPF1 to PTC-containing transcripts and, ultimately, to an increase in their decay.
insulin stimulation augments NMD of eIf4E-bound Nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)-targeted transcripts.
insulin signaling augments NMD of eif4e-bound transcripts by promoting UPF1 recruitment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insulin-mediated enhancement of eIF4F-dependent translation augments Nonsense-mediated mRNA Decay (NMD) in mammalian cells.
insulin stimulation enhances translation, which leads to the binding of NMD factors to eIF4-bound NMD substrates.
insulin signaling events augment NMD of eif4e-bound PTC-containing mRNAs by enhancing the translation of eIF4e-bound mRNAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the translation status of eIF4F-bound transcripts can modulate NMD.
insulin signaling augments NMD of eIf4E-bound Ptc-containing transcripts by enhancing translation and promoting the colocalization and association of UPF1 with PTC-containing mRNAs.
the insulin-mediated enhancement of NMD is dependent on the phosphorylation of AKT and eIF4G, and the binding of UPF1 to eIF4F.
